Let’s move into Chapter 2: Surrendering Control—Trusting God with Children’s Lives.
Once you’ve laid that foundation of prayer, the next challenge usually sneaks up on you: learning to loosen your grip on every detail of your child’s life. If you’re a parent, you know just how tough that can be. We naturally want to protect our kids—from pain, disappointment, or even just the bumps and bruises of growing up. But sometimes, that desire to shield them turns into anxiety or overprotection without us even noticing.
Here’s where the book suggests a powerful shift. Instead of hovering anxiously, it invites you to move toward faithful surrender. Now, that doesn’t mean stepping back or ignoring your child’s needs. Not at all. It’s really about recognizing where your influence ends and choosing to trust God with the things you simply can’t control or predict.
Think of it like opening your hands—letting go of worry, even when it’s hard, and allowing God to work in ways you might not see coming. And honestly, it’s not a one-and-done deal. Surrendering control is something you practice day by day. Every new season your child enters, whether it’s learning to walk, facing peer pressure as a teen, or making big decisions as an adult, brings a fresh opportunity to put this trust into action.
So, how do you actually do this? Let’s look at a few practical steps:
First, try naming your specific fears. What’s really weighing on your heart? Is it their health, their friendships, their future? When you identify those worries, it’s so much easier to bring them honestly to God in prayer.
Next, shift your prayers from asking for a particular outcome, to praying for God’s will. In other words, instead of saying, “Make this happen,” you start asking, “God, bring about what’s truly best—even if it’s not what I expect.” It’s a way of trusting that God’s understanding goes far beyond our own.
And then, after you’ve prayed, make a conscious choice to release those outcomes. Let go of the urge to micromanage every step. Instead, rest in faith that you’ve done your part, and God is at work, even in the unknowns.
Picture a parent whose child is struggling in school. The natural response might be to jump in and manage every assignment, worry about every grade. But with prayerful surrender, you might support and encourage your child, while also trusting that sometimes, growth comes from facing challenges—and that God is present through it all.
So, here’s the key takeaway: surrendering control isn’t about stepping away from your child’s life. It’s about changing your posture—from anxious striving to peaceful confidence. You’re still involved, still caring deeply, but you’re not carrying the burden alone. And that’s a huge relief. Because, in the end, God’s love and wisdom are always at work—often in ways we can’t even imagine.
